Learning Objectives
• Describe why cells are grown in the lab and that growth of cells in the lab 
is a fundamental technique for studying cells.
• Recognize and list the major types of molecules that cells can take up 
from nutrient media
• Interpret a graph of the growth of a population of cells in the lab and 
identify the general processes that are important for growth and factors 
that can inhibit growth.
• Recognize and list the things that cells need in order to grow and divide.
• Interpret a graph of the growth of a population of cells in the lab and 
identify or label the four phases of population growth of bacteria and 
eukaryotic cell lines in a liquid culture from a growth curve.
• For each phase of population growthidentify differences in the division rate and the 
survival rate.
• Distinguish between growth and division of individual cells and growth of 
a population of cells in bacteria.

Learning Objectives
• Describe the events (e.g. transcription, translation, DNA 
replication) that occur at different phases of population growth 
(of bacteria and eukaryotic cell lines) and that occur in response 
to changes in nutrients present in the environment. In order to 
do this, you will need to be able to:
• Interpret a graph of the growth of a population of cells in the lab 
and identify or label the four phases of population growth of bacteria 
and eukaryotic cell lines in a liquid culture from a growth curve.
• For each phase of population growth identify differences in the division 
rate and survival of cells.
• Describe, in general terms, how bacterial cells are grown in the lab 
and the purpose of nutrient media. (i.e. what are the components of 
media and how are they used for growth).
